evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated surgical nutrition or outside-hospital record context.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource supports this claim; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: After most uncomplicated operations, oral intake can begin early and be adapted to clinical tolerance and procedure.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Older targeted guideline; no universal postoperative feeding permission or exact hour cutoff.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated surgical nutrition or outside-hospital record context.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource supports this claim; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: Sorbitol-containing liquid medicines can contribute to diarrhea during enteral tube feeding.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Pharmacist review of replacement preparation is necessary; no drug dose equivalence or unverified crushing instructions.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated surgical nutrition or outside-hospital record context.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource supports this claim; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: Renal EN or PN formula selection should consider the calorie-to-protein ratio required by the patient.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No superiority claim for every product labeled renal.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated surgical nutrition or outside-hospital record context.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource supports this claim; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: Concentrated formulas may help selected kidney-failure patients with high nutrient needs and fluid restriction.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Individualized selection; fictional fluid allowance and formula values are not empirical targets.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated surgical nutrition or outside-hospital record context.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource supports this claim; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: For hospitalized adults with AKI or AKI on CKD during acute or critical illness who are not receiving KRT, ESPEN recommends beginning protein near 1.0 g/kg/day, then increasing toward 1.3 g/kg/day if tolerated.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Recommendation 38; the item asks for an initial prescription in acute/critical illness without KRT, not a stable outpatient CKD restriction or a universal endpoint.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinical context; see limitation.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: ESPEN identifies approximately 1.5 to 1.7 g/kg/day as the protein range for critically ill adults with AKI receiving continuous or prolonged intermittent KRT.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Recommendation 38; contextual counterfactual only. Individual tolerance, body-weight selection and the modality still require review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinical context; see limitation.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: Renal insufficiency can increase methylmalonic acid, so an elevated result is not specific evidence of B12 deficiency in a patient with reduced renal function.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Does not exclude simultaneous B12 deficiency or establish a diagnostic renal/MMA cutoff. The fictional eGFR describes the patient rather than a teaching threshold.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinical context; see limitation.
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: Swallowing impairment can differ by consistency; supervised safe oral intake can coexist with tube support when the actually consumed safe textures do not supply assessed needs.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The fictional swallow study and supervised food records establish this patient-specific boundary. Aspiration of tested liquids alone is not generalized to every texture. National and local NHS resources are related-system cross-checks, not independent trials.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinical context; see limitation.
evidenceClaims.sourceLocator: NHS overview/treatment; CUH eating and drinking during tube feeding; HEN indications
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: Guideline plus national/local public-hospital cross-checks; sources have related authority and are not independent outcome trials.

evidenceClaims.statement: The ASCOR label permits short-term IV treatment of symptomatic scurvy when oral vitamin C administration cannot provide treatment because it is not possible, insufficient or contraindicated.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not an indication for IV treatment of isolated low vitamin C without scurvy findings or for blanket postoperative wound treatment. No regimen or superiority over reliably delivered oral replacement is inferred.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinical context; see limitation.
evidenceClaims.sourceLocator: Indications and usage / limitations of use
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource; independent corroboration is not asserted.

evidenceClaims.statement: Intrinsic-factor antibody testing investigates suspected autoimmune B12 deficiency; a negative result does not exclude that cause, and normal serum B12 does not eliminate every high-suspicion case.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Local laboratory source supports the test role and uncertainty only. It does not establish an exclusive diagnostic sequence in zinc-exposed patients. No local assay cutoffs or access policies are generalized.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinical context; see limitation.
evidenceClaims.sourceLocator: Serum vitamin B12 assay; intrinsic factor antibody assay
evidenceClaims.sourceCoverageLimitation: One adequate directly verified publication/resource; independent corroboration is not asserted.

rightsDecisions.reason: Search result explicitly reserves text/data mining and AI training/similar uses. No subsequent full-text retrieval, source excerpts or claim support adopted.
Terms access returned 403; no NICE facts inferred from snippets.
PMC access showed a browser challenge; readable publisher full article and CC BY-NC notice verified.

rightsDecisions.source: Proprietary textbooks, commercial question banks, recalled exam questions

rightsDecisions.decision: four new public-sector/official-label records; six new independent atomic statements
rightsDecisions.reason: No source excerpts, figures, algorithms or tables stored. Original case tables contain fictional observations, not source tables. NHS OGL attribution recorded; manufacturer and hospital copyright kept distinct from medical authority.

limitations: Source authority is separate from reuse permissiveness.
ESPEN surgical 2025 update was identified but not used because of its rights reservation; targeted 2021 surgical facts carry an explicit currency limitation.
AuSPEN 2025 differs from older cautious-advancement practices; no universal feeding-rate/advancement or reduction rule is keyed here.
One publication counts once even if previously catalogued with multiple source IDs.
Every new source-to-claim and clinical application remains needs_clinician_review.
No empirical probabilities, demographic weights, pharmacologic dose schedules or source prose are included.

Every single-source atom explicitly records that only one adequate directly verified publication/resource supports it. Different ESPEN guidelines are different publications, not independent organizational corroboration.
